title: emergencyWithdraw does not settle accrual, redirecting the exiting user's pro-rata emissions to remaining stakers (ES-05 unchanged)
description: `emergencyWithdraw` deliberately skips `_syncBudget` and `_updatePool` (correct, per spec — the escape hatch must survive a broken dispatcher hook). However it mutates `totalStaked` and zeros out the caller's position WITHOUT first settling per-share accrual under the old denominator. On the next `_updatePool` the entire emission over `[lastRewardTime, block.timestamp]` is divided by the REDUCED `totalStaked`, so the exiting user's fair share of that interval is silently shifted onto the remaining stakers instead of being forfeited back to `rewardBudget`. This is identical to prior finding ES-05 and was not addressed by stories 001/002/003.
economicImpact: The exiting user forfeits their pending reward (intended). That reward, instead of remaining in `rewardBudget` to fund future emissions, is shifted into a higher per-share accumulator for the remaining stakers on the next accrual step. Remaining stakers receive more than their arithmetic pro-rata for the interval spanning the exit. A coordinated attacker controlling two accounts can size positions so the forfeit is captured almost entirely by a sibling account.
attackPath:
1. Attacker stakes 1000 units on account A and 1 unit on account B. `totalStaked = 1001`.
2. Time T passes; emission over T = R. No user-interaction in the interval, so `_updatePool` is not called between stake and exit.
3. Attacker calls `emergencyWithdraw()` from A. `totalStaked = 1`; A's position is zero; `_updatePool` NOT called.
4. Any subsequent user action (including B calling `claim()`) triggers `_updatePool` over the full interval `[lastRewardTime, now]`. `accRewardPerShare += (R * 1e18) / 1` — B now has pending R (approx), i.e. the whole emission over the interval.
5. B calls `claim()` and receives ~R. Under a non-attack baseline B would have received R * (1/1001).
6. Net attacker extraction: R * (1000/1001) of rewards that should have been forfeited.
quantifiedLoss: Up to `R * (exiting.amount / old_totalStaked)` per exit, where R is the emission accrued since `lastRewardTime`. `whenNotPaused` does not gate `emergencyWithdraw`, so the window of uncaptured accrual can be extended by pausing the contract (preventing other stakers from forcing an `_updatePool` via their own actions) and then un-pausing after the exit. In practice R can be days' worth of emissions if the contract was paused for a dispatcher failure.
recommendation: Call `_updatePool()` at the top of `emergencyWithdraw` (NOT `_syncBudget` — the spec correctly wants to avoid dispatcher calls here). `_updatePool` touches only internal state (no external calls), so the escape-hatch property is preserved. This settles accrual under the old denominator so the exiting user's share is left in `rewardBudget` rather than redistributed.
affectedParties: Honest stakers who happen NOT to be aligned with an emergency-withdrawing attacker; they see a silent dilution relative to arithmetic pro-rata.
profitability: Modest. Bounded by the elapsed time since the last `_updatePool` call (usually short in normal operation; potentially long if the contract has been paused). Concrete example: contract paused for 3 days at 1e18/day emission → R = 3e18; attacker sizing 1000-vs-1 extracts ~2.997e18 phUSD from the forfeit that should have gone back to budget.
